tip: ‘Yang X adalah Y’ spotlights one thing: ‘yang paling melelahkan adalah menunggu’ = the most tiring part is the waiting.
‘Jangan-jangan’ voices a worry: ‘jangan-jangan koper kita masuk ke pesawat yang salah’ = what if our suitcase got on the wrong plane.
‘Kami mohon pengertian...’ is the fixed apology formula of announcements – airports and stations use it word for word. Language you'll hear far more than speak.
‘Makan waktu’ = eats time, i.e. takes long: ‘makan waktu hampir dua jam’ = takes up almost two hours.
‘Tinggal’ + verb = all that's left is: ‘tinggal menunggu’ = just waiting now.
‘Mohon’ + ‘di-’ verb = a very polite request: ‘mohon dicek kembali’ = please check again. With hotel staff, ‘tolong dicek lagi’ is the everyday equivalent.
‘Seandainya’ = if only / supposing (unreal): ‘seandainya kami tahu’ = if we had known.
‘Turun tangan’ is literally 'lower a hand' – to step in personally: ‘manajer akhirnya turun tangan’ = the manager finally steps in himself.
‘Terlanjur’ = already done, too late to undo: ‘terlanjur membayar’ = already paid before realizing.
‘Kami kirimkan’ (‘kami’ + bare verb, no ‘meN-’) = polished service style: 'we will send it for you'. Staff language.
‘Katanya’ = they say / I heard: ‘katanya lebih sepi’ = I hear it's quieter.
‘Semakin X, semakin Y’ = the more X, the more Y: ‘semakin lama, semakin berat’ = the longer, the harder.
‘Buah tangan’ is literally 'hand fruit' – a small gift you bring back from a trip. It's the polite word; in everyday speech you'll mostly hear ‘oleh-oleh’.
‘Setengah mati’ = half dead, i.e. extremely: ‘capek setengah mati’ = dead tired.
Indonesian often gives opinions with 'according to me': ‘menurut saya’ = in my opinion. ‘Menurut’ works for any source – ‘menurut dia’, ‘menurut berita’.
‘Sekalian’ after ‘Bapak dan Ibu’ addresses the whole room: ‘Bapak dan Ibu sekalian’ = ladies and gentlemen.
‘Coba’ before a verb softens it into a suggestion: ‘kita coba dengarkan’ = let's just hear them out.
‘Mencari muka’ = to seek face, i.e. to suck up: ‘mencari muka di depan direktur’ = curry favor with the director.
‘Mohon’ + noun = a formal written request ('we request your...'), standard in office emails to superiors.
‘Sedangkan’ contrasts two halves: ‘A mendukung, sedangkan B ragu-ragu’ = A supports it, whereas B has doubts.
‘Kalau saja’ = if only (wishing things were different): ‘kalau saja tenggatnya mundur’ = if only the deadline slipped.
‘Dengan hormat’ = respectfully, the standard opener of formal letters and requests.
‘Asalkan’ = as long as, provided that: ‘asalkan tidak ada permintaan baru’ = provided nothing new is added.
‘Sedang asyik’ + verb = absorbed in doing it: ‘sedang asyik menulis’ = deep in writing.
‘Angkat tangan’ = raise your hands, i.e. give up: ‘saya angkat tangan’ = I give up.
Object + ‘saya’ + bare verb is the polished 'done by me' pattern: ‘sudah saya pindahkan’ = I have moved it.
‘Baik A maupun B’ = both A and B: ‘baik laptop lama maupun laptop baru sama-sama lambat’ = old and new laptops are equally slow.
‘Kami sampaikan bahwa...’ = the office-memo opener ('we hereby inform'); used in announcements, not in casual talk.
‘Berkecil hati’ = small-hearted, i.e. discouraged: ‘jangan berkecil hati’ = don't lose heart.
‘Pura-pura’ + verb = to pretend: ‘pura-pura sibuk membaca’ = pretending to be busy reading.
